- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- If model shows strong downward trend (e.g., 30d forecast declining steadily), true outcome often rebounds — increase forecast slope slightly to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25), model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for hidden demand or policy tailwinds.
- Model often underestimates true price volatility in early 30d horizon — increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.7% for next 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or policy uncertainty is high.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small positive spikes (e.g., 0.25, 0.33), model tends to lag — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
